text:
Logan Mailloux has been the surprise of the Blues' last two weeks. Six games into his season, he has 7 points, including three-point nights against Anaheim and New Jersey, and his role has changed with it: 19:11 a night, up from 16:46 last season, and on the ice for 41% of the power-play chances after 7%.

Our form check says the hot run is earned, in that he's getting a few more chances than usual. But the size of it is not. He's scoring 3.65 points per 60 where our range for a defenseman like him tops out near 1.4, he's shooting 20%, and six games is a small sample. Our full-season range of 20 to 36 points is the sober version.

There is a real skill underneath. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area more than 93% of defensemen last season, with 40% of his shots off the rush. Evolving-Hockey, though, had him below replacement level overall (-1.6 wins). The minutes are the thing to watch: they settle faster than the scoring will.
